messages:
Maria P: Quick spot-check across L4 / T4 / A10G for embeddings + small-chat. Short summary first: L4 lowest p50 chat latency, A10G wins embeddings throughput when using int8 quant and fused kernels, T4 is cheapest in bursty embed workloads but has higher p95 for chat. Details and numbers below.
Sam H: Nice. What batch sizes did you run for each?
Maria P: Embeddings: batch 64 & 256, small-chat (max tokens 128) with batching 8, 16, and 32. Regions: us-west1 / eu-west1 / asia-southeast1.
Priya K: Did you test INT8 vs FP16 for the three GPUs? Any quality regression on our eval set?
Maria P: Yeah — ran fp16 (baseline) and static int8 quant using our qconfig v2. Results: int8 on A10G gave ~2.2x embeddings throughput vs fp16 with ~0.6% eval RM loss; int8 on L4 showed small instability on very long prefix caching (edge cases), ~0.9% RM loss. T4 int8 was unstable in our harness (occasional NaNs), so we stuck to fp16 for T4 in chat flows.
Marco L: Kernel choices? FlashAttention vs fused_attention_v2?
Maria P: We used flash_attn on A10G and fused_attention_v2 on L4/T4 where available. On A10G flash_attn + int8 matmul path gave the biggest perf uplift for embeddings. On L4, fused_attention_v2 + kv-cache batching helped chat p50.
BenchBot: Automated summary: {us-west1 A10G embed b64 fp16: 980 qps, b256 fp16: 2100 qps; b256 int8: 4700 qps}. {L4 embed b64 fp16: 420 qps; b256 fp16: 900 qps; int8 flaky}. {T4 embed b256 fp16: 1700 qps}. Chat p50/p95 (ms): A10G fp16 b16: p50=42 p95=110; L4 fp16 b16: p50=35 p95=95; T4 fp16 b16: p50=58 p95=220.
Sam H: So L4 still best for low-latency chat. How about cost per 1M tokens?
Maria P: Rough unit econ (cloud list rates normalized): A10G fp16 embed path ~ $1.30 / 1M tok; with int8 it's ~ $0.62 / 1M tok (because effective throughput doubled+). L4 chat fp16 ~ $0.88 / 1M tok; T4 chat fp16 ~ $0.95 / 1M tok but with higher tail latency, so SLO risk. These are infra-only CPU+GPU amortized numbers, excluding network.
Priya K: Quality checks — can you drop the eval numbers? Which benchmarks?
Maria P: Eval harness: embed-sim-1k (cosine recall@10), small-chat-dialogue-2k (turn-level BLEU + human score proxy). Numbers: A10G fp16 embed recall@10 = 0.784; int8 = 0.776. Small-chat BLEU delta from fp16: A10G int8 -0.4 pts, L4 int8 -0.8 pts and some prompt corruption on 3/200 cases. So for production we shouldn't flip L4 to int8 without more calibration.
Marco L: Capacity sizing recs? If a customer needs 100k embed requests/minute in us-west1, what pool size?
Maria P: For embeddings (b256 int8 on A10G) baseline = 4700 qps -> ~282k req/min per GPU. So one A10G instance with int8 could suffice for 100k/min with headroom. For fp16 b256 on A10G it's 2100 qps -> ~126k/min so you'd need 1-2 GPUs. For L4 embeddings at fp16 you'd need ~3-4 GPUs for the same throughput.
Sam H: For small-chat with SLO p95 < 150ms, recommended config?
Maria P: Use L4 with fused kernels, batch <=16, kv-cache enabled, dedicated pool with 30% spare capacity. For bursty traffic prefer T4 only if you accept p95 > 200ms or use canary fallbacks to L4.
Priya K: Any stability issues in eu/asia regions?
Maria P: Asia (asia-southeast1) saw slightly worse network jitter affecting end-to-end wall-clock p95 (adds 10-30ms). Kernel perf was stable across regions; the perf deltas are mainly infra (rack-local NUMA) and NVLink topology differences from provider images.
Marco L: Noted. Next steps?
Maria P: Follow-ups: 1) Re-run L4 int8 with newer qcalibrator v3 to check prompt corruption; 2) Perf run with mixed-precision GEMM kernel we got from vendor; 3) Cost modeling spreadsheet update with these numbers. I'll drop the CSV to #eng-ml later.
Sam H: Please tag me when you drop the CSV. Also add the raw logs from bench runs to the s3 bucket path.
Maria P: Will do. CSV + raw logs -> s3://redwood-bench/compact-spotcheck/1777777777/
Priya K: Thanks, useful snapshot. :rocket:
